main_strengths: Rich, mostly correct Austrian vocabulary: malinvestment, Cantillon effects, structure of production, time preference, forbearance/liquidation, sound money
Very good fit on events that are themselves interventions or credit busts (YCC, assisted bank merger, China infrastructure stimulus, stablecoin run, interbank stress, EM peg)
Historical analogs are almost all real, pre-2025 and appropriately chosen (1907, 1920s-30s, 1970s, Japan 1990s, Asia 1997, GFC, BoJ YCC 2016)
Tool-use format is consistent and parseable; snapshot echoed correctly in get_macro_data observations
main_problems: Signal collapse: equities SHORT, gold LONG and credit SHORT in 20/20 items (gold conviction 4-5 every time); bonds never LONG; this is a teacher default, not event-driven

Every event, including positive shocks (payroll beat, GDP beat, productivity jump, tariff truce), is forced into 'reveals malinvestment -> liquidation'; the student will learn that Austrians are perma-bears
School-logic error on trade: tariff truce called 'another intervention', when removing tariffs is pro-market in Austrian terms
Scenario block is templated: always 4 scenarios, top prob 0.35-0.45, near-identical labels (Delayed liquidation / Necessary liquidation / Sound-money reset)

Signals often contradict own scenarios: bonds SHORT under debt-deflation, USD NEUTRAL/SHORT where yen/sterling/dollar-funding logic implies otherwise, 'contained/reflation' scenarios with no effect on signals
Non-US events (BoE, RBA, BoJ, China, frontier EM) analysed with a US-style snapshot and US asset signals with no acknowledgment; no local currency or local-bond view
Snapshot values are cited before get_macro_data is called in most items, making the tool call redundant

Minor fabricated observations ('rising unemployment' with no time series) and stretched readings (HY 430-480bp called stress, 1.6% CPI with 4.4% GDP called fragile); 1920-21 depression mischaracterised
suggested_prompt_or_template_changes: Require the teacher to first classify the event's sign for the economy (positive/negative/ambiguous) and whether it adds or removes intervention, and make signals conditional on it; give explicit Austrian examples of bullish or neutral outcomes (deregulation, tariff removal, rate normalisation, genuine saving-driven growth, productivity gains)

Rebalance with a rejection/quota rule: cap the share of identical signal vectors (e.g. reject if equities SHORT + gold LONG + credit SHORT exceeds ~50% per batch), and require each signal to cite a specific chain step

Allow 2-4 scenarios with free labels and require that the highest-probability scenario determine the sign of the signals; add a check that bonds/USD signals match debt-deflation vs inflationary scenarios
Make the macro snapshot match the event's economy (or label it 'US/global backdrop' and add a local-currency / local-bond signal for non-US events)
Enforce tool ordering: the first Think may not reference snapshot numbers before get_macro_data is observed (or drop the snapshot from the user prompt)
Forbid claims about trends ('rising unemployment', 'credit tightening') that a single-point snapshot cannot show, unless stated in the event
Generate internally consistent snapshots (e.g. policy rate vs 10y vs 2s10s, frontier inflation events with matching CPI/M2) or have the teacher explicitly note inconsistencies
Add a few hand-written gold trajectories for positive shocks and pro-market policy events to anchor fidelity without perma-bear bias
